dramatic_truth: Alder Basin spill forces a detour through industrial ropewalk and North Glass Cut, where Greg succeeds by following specialists through dangerous visual and infrastructure conditions rather than trying to lead.
performance: He asks only route-relevant questions, lets official field readers own Four-C and Cut conditions, adapts crutch geometry to grate and switchback, and uses lock-in only when a marker response compresses time enough to justify it.
screenplay: Field reader reports partial Four-C charge; ropewalk detour; freight cage stops but existing repair fixes it; narrow switchback and stairs; North Glass Cut afterimage route; marker response creates brief lock-in; crew clears Cut.
prose_comparison: The procedural sequence is the embodied meaning of follower: expertise is distributed and Greg's competence is knowing whose line to follow.

dramatic_truth: At the first real road camp north of Glass Cut, Greg learns field life includes long uneventful travel, maintenance delays, ordinary watches, mice, and one reed hound that leaves when told no.
performance: He lets local farmers and road workers own route problems, accepts camp chores, takes watch without dramatizing it, and uses logistics rather than combat against minor animal pressure.
screenplay: Hostile wagon ride; orchard detour; long quiet road; camp setup under Pella Dorn; glass mice defeated by moving soap and noise; lone reed hound watches and withdraws; watch passes normally.
prose_comparison: The quiet repetition is the point: adventure becomes inhabited routine rather than a chain of escalating incidents.

dramatic_truth: Greg records West Locks behavior while crossing active regional infrastructure, and his magic becomes deliberately practical in a tiny unauthorized save without displacing lock procedure.
performance: He documents false tones and custody exactly, catches a sliding brass tag with one external push, records the attempt as non-procedure, and treats success as evidence rather than permission.
screenplay: East gallery and false lock tone; West Five cargo cradle; custody tag slides toward grate; Greg deliberately alters path by external effect; marsh crossing and signal-station work continue under existing authority.
prose_comparison: The infrastructure detail makes the tiny magic success legible as transfer from training into life, while keeping it proportionate.

dramatic_truth: At North Station Greg becomes a practitioner by combining field record discipline, current-body movement, and increasingly usable magic without turning any one success into a general rule.
performance: He records signal-arm drift, accepts separate controlled magic questions for later, and keeps road work primary over experimentation.
screenplay: Dask interrogates prior tag push; mast arm moves against wind; route logs and manual confirmation continue; Greg's practical magic history becomes explicit crew context without becoming job credential.
prose_comparison: The chapter integrates magic practice into ordinary field identity instead of creating a training interlude detached from work.

dramatic_truth: Three Posts appears abandoned, then a human scream forces Greg back into combat mode to recover three station workers from reed hounds.
performance: Vessa explicitly authorizes Greg to direct movement while retaining abort authority; Greg uses old tactical timing through current crutch geometry, attempts one ambiguous external effect, and stops once people are recovered rather than hunting animals.
screenplay: Incomplete ledger and missing staff; fresh tracks and empty sheath; scream; three workers found under hound pressure; Greg/Kel/Maro advance; crutch fighting and mud; one ambiguous paw-target magic attempt; group extraction; mundane explanation resolves apparent mystery.
prose_comparison: The fight earns its detailed physical rhythm because it is the first serious test of old combat timing inside the changed body and distributed crew command.

dramatic_truth: The morning after the hound fight makes Greg pay the bodily cost of competence and accept patient status while the survey route continues around him.
performance: He inventories pain honestly, accepts medical evaluation and load restrictions, protects permission around his damaged crutch, and recognizes current-body techniques are not merely inherited first-life skill.
screenplay: Shoulder/palm assessment; crutch bite inspection; med hand Jessa Ril bounds likely strain; Pellin evacuated; route resumes under manual signal confirmation; Greg travels under reduced load rather than pretending recovery.
prose_comparison: The recovery detail is necessary consequence, preventing combat competence from becoming costless and deepening current-body ownership.

dramatic_truth: At Lark Spur Greg deliberately buys an obsolete eight-copper line quietener because he can afford its known problem, not because the region's false-tone issue proves special hidden value.
performance: He asks for failure history and bench-use conditions, bargains without magical thinking, accepts that the tool suppresses weak true tones as well as false ones, and keeps it personal rather than field equipment.
screenplay: Shoulder still restricted; retired hardware table; line quietener documentation and bargaining; eight-copper purchase leaves fifteen; crew leaves toward Greyhook under strict non-use terms.
prose_comparison: The acquisition completes the capital-discipline thesis: Greg buys a constrained problem with known downside rather than a miracle.

dramatic_truth: A Greyhook weather hold becomes maintenance day for Greg's body, crutch, and new line quietener, proving useful things stay useful through repair and bounded testing.
performance: Rusk repairs the hound-bitten crutch under assignment coverage; Tala permits a bench-only quietener comparison; Greg stops once the known use and known downside are demonstrated rather than turning the yard into research lab.
screenplay: Wind hold; crutch resin/fiber repair; retired quietener tested on short copper bench; short-delay echo damped but weak true strike also suppressed; longer-delay behavior differs once; owner wraps it and stops.
prose_comparison: Maintenance and bench testing change equipment state and establish exactly why the tool is useful and dangerous.

dramatic_truth: Greg crosses Greyhook's exposed North Reach under a clean weather window, proving current-body route competence without hiding shoulder limits or relying on emergency chain infrastructure.
performance: He uses shelter timing, contact-first stair movement, declared rests, and local warnings; a four-breath dead-air pocket is logged but not investigated mid-ridge.
screenplay: Three towers hold green; exposed crown crossing; shelters and gossip; loose chain bypass; silent high-wind section; brief dead pocket; North Gate arrival and equipment handoff.
prose_comparison: The crossing is embodied travel progression. The repeated markers, gusts, shelters, and rests are the route itself, not redundant atmosphere.

dramatic_truth: At North Reach Greg chooses hot water, recovery, and then another northward extension toward White Span, showing that home can pull on him without making farther movement a mistake.
performance: He buys one copper of recovery and stops there, keeps personal experimental gear out of the new river question, and chooses the Lume route only after crew and regional authority frame it as observational continuity.
screenplay: Hot bath; North Reach briefing; wrong-direction sunrise reflection on Lume River creates extension option; crew agrees; Greg chooses north; road to Kettle Vale; local observation plan prepared for dawn White Span.
prose_comparison: The chapter is a transition of belonging, recovery, and chosen extension. Its quietness is the emotional payoff to the road arc.
